docs.summary:
Arbitration bus for interactive scene-view handles. Every handle reports how far it is from the cursor via [`AddControl`](#api~Prowl.Editor.GUI.SceneView.HandleContext~AddControl); the nearest one wins and may take the drag.

One instance per scene viewport, owned by the panel. The frame model is a single pass: registrations accumulate all frame and resolve at the next [`BeginFrame`](#api~Prowl.Editor.GUI.SceneView.HandleContext~BeginFrame), so handles act on the previous pass's winner. Because [`Hot`](#api~Prowl.Editor.GUI.SceneView.HandleContext~Hot) outranks [`Nearest`](#api~Prowl.Editor.GUI.SceneView.HandleContext~Nearest) for the whole of a drag, the one-frame lag only ever affects hover highlighting and the initial press.

Resolution happens in [`BeginFrame`](#api~Prowl.Editor.GUI.SceneView.HandleContext~BeginFrame) rather than [`EndFrame`](#api~Prowl.Editor.GUI.SceneView.HandleContext~EndFrame) so that controls registered from deferred draw callbacks - which run after the input pass - still take part.
Distance to register for a large body region (a rect interior, say) so it beats the default control but loses to any real handle the cursor is actually near.

Screen distances within this many pixels of each other count as overlapping, and the tie is settled by depth instead. Without a band, two handles stacked at the same screen point would be ordered by sub-pixel projection noise rather than by which one is actually in front.

Viewport rect in absolute Paper space. Projection and all handle distances use this space because it is the space the overlay canvas draws in, so a handle's pick region and its drawn shape stay in agreement.
Viewport dimensions in pixels.
Cursor in absolute Paper space. All handle distances are measured against this.
Cursor relative to the viewport's top-left, for camera ray and picking helpers.
Camera navigation is in progress: nothing may pick or start a drag.

A UI widget is consuming typing this frame (a text field is being edited). Scene-view keyboard shortcuts must stand down, or typing "d" into an inspector field also duplicates whatever the scene editor has selected.
Key-down that yields to text editing. Use this instead of [`Input`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Input) directly for any scene-view shortcut.
Key-held that yields to text editing. See [`GetKeyDown`](#api~Prowl.Editor.GUI.SceneView.HandleContext~GetKeyDown).

Cursor shape requested by handles this frame, or [`Inherit`](#api~Prowl.PaperUI.PaperCursor~Inherit) when none asked. The viewport applies it to its own element, so Paper resolves it exactly like any UI hover cursor rather than fighting it.

members.name: AddControl
members.signature: public void AddControl(ControlID id, float screenDistance, float depth = float.MaxValue)

docs.summary:
Report this control's screen-space distance from the cursor, in pixels, and how far in front of the camera it sits. The nearest control on screen wins; controls whose screen distances are within [`DepthTieBandPixels`](#api~Prowl.Editor.GUI.SceneView.HandleContext~DepthTieBandPixels) of each other count as overlapping and are settled by `depth` instead, so a handle behind another cannot steal the cursor. Exact ties go to the later registration, so register smaller and more specific handles last.

`MaxValue` (and any non-finite value) as the distance means "not a candidate this frame", so a handle that is simply not under the cursor can report unconditionally rather than the caller having to branch around the call.

Leaving `depth` unset means "depth unknown", which loses every overlap tie to a control that does report one. Screen-space overlays that always draw on top should pass 0.

docs.summary: Register a point handle at a world position, deriving both its screen distance and its depth. The preferred overload for anything anchored in the scene, since it cannot forget the depth.
Register a fallback that wins only when no other control registered at all.
True when this control should render as hovered or active: it owns the drag, or nothing owns a drag and it is the nearest.
Take the drag if this control won arbitration and the primary button just went down.
Release the drag if this control owns it and the primary button came up.

docs.summary: Whether the cursor has travelled far enough since the grab to count as a drag rather than a click. Used to let a press inside a body either move it or fall through to selection.
Combined projection * view for this frame, for callers that project themselves.
Deferred 3D drawing, replayed onto the viewport overlay after the input pass.
Project a world point into viewport-local pixels. Null when behind the camera.

How far in front of the camera a world point sits, along the view direction. Used to settle overlapping handles; smaller is nearer. Negative behind the camera. Measured along the view axis rather than as a straight-line distance, so handles at the edge of a wide viewport are not treated as further away than ones at its centre.

docs.summary: Screen distance from the cursor to a world point, or `MaxValue` when the point is behind the camera or further away than `grabRadiusPixels`.
docs.remarks: The radius is a grab region, not a bias: outside it the handle is not a candidate at all. Returning a real distance at any range would make every registered handle outrank the viewport's default control no matter how far from the cursor it sat, which silently disables object picking.
